draft.title: How purpose shapes structure
card: A text is organised to do a job. Its purpose decides how its parts are ordered.
Narrative
entertains with a story. It usually moves from an opening that introduces characters and setting, through a problem, to a resolution.
Information report
gives facts about a topic. It usually has an opening statement, then paragraphs or sections that each cover one part of the topic.
Procedure
explains how to do something. It usually lists the materials, then gives numbered steps in time order.
draft.remember: Ask what a text is for, and its structure will usually follow.

a.q: Why is a procedure usually written as numbered steps in order?
opts: The reader has to do each action in the right sequence
The reader needs a problem and a resolution to enjoy
The reader wants facts sorted into topic sections
The reader should be shown several sides of an argument
a.why: A procedure helps someone do a task, so the order of actions matters. Sorting facts into sections suits an information report, which has a different job.
a.clue: Think about what the reader does with the text.

b.q: Jess writes about the life of the platypus. She starts with a short statement of what a platypus is. Then she writes one paragraph on its habitat, one on its diet and one on its body. Which text type is she writing?
opts: An information report
A narrative
A procedure
A diary of events
b.why: An opening statement followed by paragraphs that each cover one part of a topic is the structure of an information report. A narrative would follow characters through a problem, and a procedure would give steps.
b.clue: Look at how the paragraphs are sorted.

a.best: The reader has to do each action in the right sequence

proposal.title: How purpose shapes structure
card: Narrative
tells a story to entertain. It usually moves from an opening that introduces characters and setting, through a problem, to a resolution.
Information report
gives facts about a topic. It usually has an opening statement, then paragraphs or sections that each cover one part of the topic.
Persuasive text
tries to win the reader over to a point of view. It usually states its position, gives one argument per paragraph with reasons, then restates the position.
Procedure
explains how to do something. It usually lists the materials, then gives numbered steps in time order, because the reader follows them while doing the task.
proposal.remember: A text's job shapes its structure: a story, facts by topic, arguments or steps.
